courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Cathedrals, Abbeys, Castles: Gothic Art and Architecture (c. 1130-1450)
courses.description: The seminar explores Gothic church and secular art and architecture in France and Europe between c. 1130 and c.1450. It focuses not only on the formal and artistic progresses in architecture, sculpture, and stained glass windows during this period, but also on the social, political, and economic aspects of medieval society that affected these developments.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Art, War, and Revolution
courses.description: Focusing on one or two works of art per week in a variety of media, this course explores the complex relationship between art, war, and conflict in the modern world. Honors version available.

source.text: ARTH 54. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-PAST.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Art, Gender, and Power in Early Modern Europe
courses.description: This first-year seminar introduces students to some of the issues related to representations of western European men and women in the period 1400-1700. Portraits, mythological and biblical imagery, and even architecture will be studied for their attention to gender. Honors version available.

source.text: ARTH 55. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-PAST.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Lives of East Asian Artworks at the Ackland Art Museum
courses.description: This course traces the "lives" of East Asian artworks as to how they entered the Ackland Art Museum, transformed, and became part of its collection, as well as related issues. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: World's Fairs
courses.description: This first-year seminar focuses on the constructed images of the modern American city. We have selected six U.S. World's Fairs between 1893 and 1965 (1884 World Cotton Centennial, New Orleans; 1893 World's Colombian Exposition, Chicago; 1904 Louisiana Purchase Exposition, Saint Louis; 1939 New York World's Fair, New York City; 1962 Seattle World's Fair; 1964/1965 New York World's Fair). By examining them in detail, we can follow shifts in conceptions of cities (and the world).

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: African American Art of the Carolinas
courses.description: This course explores the visual arts created by African Americans living and working in the Carolinas from the era of plantation slavery through the 20th century.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Picturing Nature
courses.description: This seminar focuses on how the collecting and study of natural and aesthetic wonders shaped ideas about knowledge in the arts and sciences.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Art, Money, and the Market
courses.description: This seminar explores the complex relationship between art and economy in the age of capitalism, focusing on artworks that interpret market activities and address the subject of economic value.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Art and Astronomy: 3000 BCE to Present
courses.description: For millennia, people have gazed into the universe and wondered about their place in it. How did the universe begin, what is its nature, and how do its cycles shape human lives? This seminar considers how artwork reflects human efforts to address these questions, from the earliest recorded observations by Sumerians to present; how ancient peoples around the world observed and understood the cosmos; how maps, clocks, and methods of measurement have changed over time and made long-distance travel possible; how clashes between competing worldviews altered traditional conceptions of space and time; and how we explore our own nature.

source.text: ARTH 75. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-PAST.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Art and Technology
courses.description: This course examines the relationships between the history of technology and artistic practice. Our conception of "technology" is broad, extending beyond mere tools to include a host of apparatuses and their relationships to perception, experience, representation, and communication. This course will explore the impacts of technological innovation on society and culture, and vice versa, along with the ways in which artists have addressed, responded to, and critiqued technological progress and invention.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Content varies by semester. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art and Death
courses.description: The course covers medieval/early modern artifacts connected to the phenomenon of death as well as the diversity of donations for individual commemoration in Europe. It will explore the social, political, and economic aspects of the societies that affected these phenomena. Invited speakers will open up the perspective to other cultures and time periods.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: The Art of Animals: Africa and Beyond
courses.description: This class views the relationship between humans and animals through works of art. Drawing examples from cultures across the world, we address animals as symbols of leadership, beauty, and extraordinary powers. Elephants, leopards, spiders, and dogs of all kinds, along with many other mammals, reptiles, birds, and insects will be studied.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art and Sports in the Americas
courses.description: Representations of sports tell us a lot about artistic, historic, and contemporary Latin America, the Caribbean, and the United States. This course focuses on depictions of sports in these regions and the varied meanings they communicate.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: The Visual World
courses.description: The visual world surrounds us in print and moving images, in virtual realities and in physical space. This course gives students the tools to analyze, research, and historicize images and objects. How does the visual domain inform our understanding of the world around us? How do they shape culture, knowledge, and identity? Each week, key concerns of the present from technology to climate change are explored through art and artifacts of the past. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: History of Western Art I
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the historical development of art in the Mediterranean basin, from the end of the Prehistoric Period to the Medieval Period, from a Western perspective, and also an introduction to the history of art as a discipline. As we consider selected cultures and monuments in their larger archaeological, art-historical, and historical context, we will develop visual skills through the formal analysis of works of art. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art in Life: An Introduction to Western Art from the Renaissance to the Modern Period
courses.description: This is the second semester of the two-semester survey course including Western art and visual culture from the Renaissance to the modern period. ARTH 151 is not a prerequisite for ARTH 152 . Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: African Art Survey
courses.description: Africa is both the past and the future of art making: the earliest known art by humans was created there, and African artists are featured in major exhibitions all over the world. This introduction to African art will address many types of art (including sculpture, painting, architecture, textiles, and masquerades) in many different social contexts (ceremony, politics, royalty, domestic arenas, cross-cultural exchanges, colonialism, postcolonialism, the international art world). We will visit the African art collection at the Ackland Museum of Art.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Architecture
courses.description: What is architecture? What does it do? This course is designed to encourage students to consider architecture less as something technical, existing in a separate sphere from everyday life, but as social space.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Introduction to East Asian Art and Architecture
courses.description: This course traces the history of art and architecture in premodern East Asia, emphasizing ideas and ways of seeing and representing that were common or different across East Asia.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: The Film Experience: Introduction to the Visual Study of Film
courses.description: A critical and historical introduction to film from a visual arts perspective. The course surveys the history of film from its inception to the present, drawing upon both foreign and American traditions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Introduction to the Art and Architecture of Pre-Hispanic Mesoamerica
courses.description: This course introduces the art, architecture, and cultures of Pre-Hispanic Mesoamerica, from the rise of Mesoamerica's first high civilization in the second millennium BCE to the defeat of the Aztec Empire in 1521 CE. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Introduction to American Art
courses.description: This course surveys American art, architecture, and material culture from early European exploration of the Americas to the 1960s. Previously offered as ARTH 261.

source.text: ARTH 161. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST, FAD.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Pencils to Pixels: The History of Animation
courses.description: This course examines the history and development of animation as an art form and an industry worldwide. It covers early experiments with animation, the transition to sound and feature films, and the rise of classical Hollywood studios. Course material will extend to other countries or regions. Work created outside the industry, such as experimental, cult, fine art, and video game animation, will also be considered. The course will track the development of the technology and techniques of animation, such as cel animation, stop-motion animation, puppet animation, silhouette animation, rotoscoping, pixilation, direct animation, limited animation on TV, and computer animation.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Special Topics in Art History, FC-AESTH
courses.description: Selected topics in art history.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art and Fashion from Rome to Timbuktu
courses.description: In the Roman Empire and in contemporary Africa, clothing reflects local symbolic systems and global trade networks. Rome is imagined as the source of Western culture, and Africa evokes distant exoticism; this course will complicate such conceptions. Through fashion we explore political, economic, and religious systems, as well as creativity.

source.text: ARTH 200. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-GLOBAL. | CLAR 200 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Making Material Histories: A Makerspace Course
courses.description: This course explores the history and technology of materials from wood and glass to steel and plastic in art, culture, and science. Students will engage with materials both through hands-on fabrication at BeAM and through researching historical debates surrounding material invention and use by artists, scientists, and industries.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: The Visual Culture of News, Past and Present
courses.description: Focusing on Western news production from early modernity to the present, this class considers the news as a visual object, examining the different formats and media of news, the design of the page/pamphlet/screen, the way images are incorporated, and the relationship of all of this to written text.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art and Archaeology of the Ancient Near East
courses.description: A survey of the cultures of the ancient Near East, Mesopotamia, Anatolia (modern Turkey), and the Levant, from the first settled villages of the ninth millennium to the Persian conquest of Babylon in 539 BCE.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Empires of the Nile: The Archaeology of Egypt and Nubia
courses.description: A survey of the archaeological remains of ancient Egypt and Nubia, from late prehistory through the first millennium BCE.

source.text: ARTH 242. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | CLAR 242 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Greek Art and Archaeology
courses.description: The historical development of the art and architecture of Greece from the Bronze Age through the Hellenistic period.

source.text: ARTH 244. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | CLAR 244 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Roman Art and Archaeology
courses.description: This course explores the archaeology of the Roman world between the eighth century BCE and the fifth century CE, focusing on issues of urbanization, trade and consumption, colonization, and the Roman army.

source.text: ARTH 247. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | CLAR 247 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Objects, Museums, and Meanings
courses.description: This course explores objects and meaning in the context of museums. How does one "read" an object? What do works of art communicate on their own, and how do a series of decisions - made by individuals and institutions - shape how we understand them? Through museum visits, object-based learning and research, readings, and discussion, this course will consider how objects, and their collection and display, shape our understanding of the world around us. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art History in Motion: Looking, Hearing, Sensing
courses.description: This class investigates bringing awareness to the way we move and our sensorial experiences as vital complements to other methodological approaches to art historical interpretation. It does so through an examination of a variety of artworks in their historical contexts, different movement explorations, and analysis of interpretative methods. Attending both to art and ourselves in this way, we can question, challenge, and expand the ways in which we know the world. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Women in the Visual Arts I
courses.description: This course analyzes the role of women in Western art as art producers and consumers of art and looks at how women have been represented.

source.text: ARTH 254. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | WGST 254 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: African Art and Culture
courses.description: African art is deeply embedded in African societies, past and present. Artistic practices are integral to politics, religion, social status, economics, and self-expression. The course explores masquerades, sculpture, architecture, dress, rural and urban arts, and contemporary practices to understand how art functions as a dynamic social and cultural force. We will view artworks at the Ackland Art Museum, and we will invite artists and scholars to visit our class in person and/or via zoom.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Chinese Art and Culture: From Song to Qing
courses.description: Organized around eight key themes, the course highlights the multifaceted character and vibrant textures of Chinese art from the Song dynasty (960-1279) to the Qing dynasty (1644-1912). Students will study canonized genres--landscape representation, court and literati practices--while also engaging with topics often marginalized in survey narratives, including depictions of animals and the varied roles women assumed within artistic worlds.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Medieval Art in Western Europe
courses.description: Survey of major developments in painting and sculpture in Europe during the Latin Middle Ages (300-1400 CE).

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Medieval Iconography
courses.description: Required preparation, any introductory art history course or permission of the instructor. Understanding the meaning of medieval art by examining the iconography of selected important works. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: From Alexander to Cleopatra: Hellenistic Art and Archaeology
courses.description: Survey of the archaeology of the Hellenistic Mediterranean from the time of Alexander the Great until the Roman conquest (350-31 BCE), with emphasis on art and architecture of cities and sanctuaries.

source.text: ARTH 268. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | CLAR 268 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Cathedrals, Abbeys, Castles: Gothic Art and Architecture (c. 1130-1450)
courses.description: This course covers the development of Gothic church and secular architecture in Europe between 1130 and 1500. It explores the formal and constructive progress in architecture (including its decoration: sculpture, stained glass windows) as well as the social, political, and economic aspects of medieval society that affected these developments.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Northern European Art: Van Eyck to Bruegel
courses.description: Required preparation, any introductory art history course or permission of the instructor. Survey of painting and sculpture ca. 1400-1600 in the Netherlands--Belgium (Flanders) and Holland--as well as France and England.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: European Baroque Art
courses.description: Required preparation, any introductory art history course or permission of the instructor. This course examines 17th-century art and architecture in Europe.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: 18th-Century Art
courses.description: An introductory survey of 18th century European visual culture, from painting and sculpture to art markets and the decorative arts. This class works closely with art objects in person at the Ackland Museum of Art and Wilson Special Collections. Central themes in the class include Europe's relationship to the world, the sociology of the art world, and how art objects are made.

source.text: ARTH 275. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art and Architecture of Viceregal Latin America
courses.description: This course surveys the art and architecture of Hispanophone and Lusophone America of the Viceregal period (1492-ca. 1810).

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: The Arts in England, 1450-1650
courses.description: This course explores the visual culture of England during the reigns of the Tudors and Stuarts. This will include portraits of Henry VIII, Elizabeth I, and Charles I by artists such as Holbein, Van Dyck, and Rubens, royal palaces, printed books, tomb monuments, heraldry, spectacles, as well as portraits of the middle classes. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Picture That: History of Photography from Tintypes to Instagram
courses.description: This course presents a select history of photography from its invention to its most recent manifestations. Global in its orientation, this course is designed thematically rather than chronologically to develop dialogues between places and ideas.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art of Exchange and Exploration: Early America and the Globe
courses.description: This course offers a transnational look at American visual culture. It considers the encounters, exchanges, and circulations of art, artists, and ideas across boundaries and oceans from the colonial eighteenth century to the Civil War.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Modern Art in Europe 1850-1900: Realism, Impressionism, Post-Impressionism
courses.description: The development of European art from 1850 to 1905, with an emphasis on French avant-garde movements including realism and impressionism, as well as international movements such as symbolism and art nouveau.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Picturing Paris: 1800-2000
courses.description: This class explores the cultural, political, and artistic circumstances in which images of Paris have been made and viewed, as well as various visual technologies that have disseminated and marketed.

source.text: ARTH 283. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Modern Art in Europe 1900-1960: Avant-Gardes and Politics
courses.description: Major figures, movements, and themes of modernism from cubism and the emergence of abstraction to the transfer of artistic energy and innovation to the United States after World War II.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art Since 1960
courses.description: This course will explore some of the major trends in American and European art, covering a range of provocative objects, ideas, and practices that continue to resonate. It provides a basis for understanding and assessing contemporary art, in relation to various historical, social, cultural, and political contexts. This course presents contemporary art and discourse as diverse, contradictory, contested, and unresolved. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: African American Art Survey
courses.description: An introduction to African American art and artists and their social contexts from early slavery.

source.text: ARTH 287. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | AAAD 237 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Special Topics in Art History
courses.description: Required preparation, any introductory art history course or permission of the instructor. Selected topics in art history.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art, Culture, and Power in Africa
courses.description: This course explores how power operates through objects in Africa, including royal regalia, objects used in healing and other ritual contexts, and African art as commodity in international markets.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art History Practicum
courses.description: Students complete an internship in an art history related field. Students will gain practical knowledge of the practice of art history. Studio majors may use this course to fulfill an art history requirement by pursuing faculty-approved, nonpaid internships working in nonprofit or commercial art sectors.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Arts of Southern Africa
courses.description: This course focuses on a wide range of regions, time periods, and genres in the visual arts in southern Africa, including archaeological materials, arts associated with longstanding indigenous cultures, art that reflects the often violent encounter with European cultures, and contemporary arts that are produced in the region today.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Clothing and Textiles in Africa
courses.description: This class explores how dress reveals information about African aesthetics, culture, and history, including its roles in political systems, religious worship, fashion trends, and other aspects of social life.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Arts of West Africa
courses.description: This course addresses the roles of art in the lives of West Africans who make and use it, spanning centuries of African creativity from archaeological sites to 21st-century artists.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art of African Independence
courses.description: This course focuses on African art produced in the mid-twentieth century. It promotes comparative analysis around themes of modernity, nationalism, independence, identity, and the role of the artist in society.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Fashioning Identities
courses.description: This course examines fashion and the political, social, and cultural discourses, conditions, and institutional formations used in the creation of varied social and personal identities.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art and Colonialism: France in Africa/Africa in France
courses.description: Art elucidates French and African experiences of colonial rule, as a record of political transformations and a tool for resistance and the assertion of local cultures.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Islam and African Art
courses.description: People everywhere use works of art to facilitate worship, to depict spirits, and to celebrate their beliefs. Islam, a major religion in Africa, is no exception. This course focuses on Islam in African visual arts.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Loving Your Local Art Scene
courses.description: This course takes students on a tour of Chapel Hill, Carrboro, Durham, and Raleigh's grassroots visual arts scenes, exploring everything from commercial galleries to artist-run non-profits to craft fairs to artists' studios. We will use our local arts scene as a case study to map out how art worlds function. Students' final assignment is to contribute to an ongoing digital web-based - an interactive local arts map. This class is especially beneficial for student artists.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: From Charlemagne to Bauhaus: German Art and Architecture from the Middle Ages to Modern Time
courses.description: The course focuses on art and architecture in the German-speaking countries (Germany, Switzerland, Austria and in regions formerly belonging to the historical Holy Roman Empire) from Charlemagne in the eighth century to the Bauhaus in the 1920s and beyond. It studies the artistic developments and exchanges with neighboring countries (such as France, Italy, etc.) over the centuries and discusses them in the relevant historical and political contexts.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Chinese Landscape Representation in the Second Millennium
courses.description: This course delves into the theme of landscape, or "mountains and waters" (shanshui), which has been a central subject of artistic expression in China since the tenth century. We will explore a selection of landscape paintings from the tenth century through to the early eighteenth century. Students will be introduced to key interpretive approaches for understanding and examining landscapes as both artistic and social entities in pre-modern China.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art, History, and the Modern Museum
courses.description: Focusing on art, history, and ethnography museums in Europe and North America, this course considers the emergence and development of museums as powerful social and cultural institutions from the mid-18th century to the 21st century. A variety of perspectives on museums showcase their connections to larger political and cultural trends.

source.text: ARTH 330. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST, RESEARCH. | HIST 320 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: The Art of Dying Well: Death and Commemoration in the Middle Ages and Early Modern Times
courses.description: Covers medieval and early modern artifacts and monuments connected with death as well as the diversity of donations for individual commemoration. Explores the social, political, and economic aspects of medieval/early modern society that affected these developments and phenomena.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Saints in Medieval Art
courses.description: This course will explore the modes in which saints and issues related to sainthood are visualized in medieval art.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Late Medieval Art
courses.description: This course explores the art of the late medieval period in Byzantium and the Latin West.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: The Renaissance Portrait
courses.description: This course focuses on European portraits produced in the period c. 1400-1600. Through careful study of specific paintings, prints, and sculptures, by artists such as Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Albrecht Dürer, we will explore different ways of interpreting portraiture in the Renaissance, addressing issues of identity, reception, and function.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: European Art and Sexuality
courses.description: Between 1400 and 1600, major European artists (Hieronymus Bosch, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Titian, Dürer) made radical contributions to the representation of the sexual body. This course will use Northern European and Italian art as a lens for investigating Early Modern approaches to the figuration of sexuality and gender.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Visual Art in the Age of Revolution
courses.description: This course examines the visual culture that participated in revolutions in Europe and the world from circa 1770 to 1850.

source.text: ARTH 370. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Life and Art in Ancient Pompeii
courses.description: In this course we will explore the history and archaeology of Pompeii with the goal of better understanding daily life in the early Roman empire. The course proceeds topically, moving from an exploration of the city's public spaces to an analysis of more private domains--houses, gardens, and tombs. We will also consider evidence from ancient literature and epigraphy. Students may not receive credit for both CLAR 380 and CLAS 73.

source.text: ARTH 380. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | CLAR 380 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Everything You Ever Wanted to Know About Modern Architecture But Were Afraid to Ask
courses.description: Required preparation, any introductory art history course or permission of the instructor. This course will examine the history of architecture from the early 19th century to the present.

source.text: ARTH 383. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Pop Art and Its Legacy
courses.description: This course will investigate what is commonly termed "pop art." We will examine the various issues at stake in the appropriation of mass media imagery and techniques, the diversity within the movement, the different arguments surrounding particular artists and artworks, and pop art's continuing legacy in work by contemporary artists.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: 20th-Century African American Art
courses.description: Focus on the historical development of African American art from the Harlem Renaissance of early 20th century through the Black Arts Movement and Feminist Art Movement 1960s and early 1970s.

source.text: ARTH 387. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | AAAD 330 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Special Topics in Art History
courses.description: Required preparation, any intermediate art history course or permission of the instructor. Selected topics in art history.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Undergraduate Research Seminar
courses.description: This is the capstone course for art history majors. Required preparation, art history major and junior standing or permission of the instructor. The field and theme of the course change according to the instructor's area of expertise. The seminar introduces students to research in art history and involves an original research project culminating in a substantial research paper.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Directed Readings in Art History
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Independent study under the direction of a faculty member.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Special Topics in Art History, FC-AESTH
courses.description: Required preparation, any intermediate art history course or permission of the instructor. Selected topics in art history.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: German and Netherlandish Renaissance
courses.description: The course focuses on a crucial period of German and Netherlandish art around 1500, referred to as the so-called Age of Dürer, which still shows influences of Gothic art but also of new Italian Renaissance. Often based on artifacts of the Ackland Art Museum, case studies explore the interaction of artists and patrons in important art centers of the time.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Seen, Unseen, and Suggested: Representation and Hollywood Film Censorship
courses.description: This course will look at the history of film censorship in the United States from the perspective of how such things as the Production Code (Hays Code), wartime restrictions, Anti-communist blacklisting, regional and local censorship boards (for example, Southern Baptist Ministers prior to 1968), late 1960s movements for social change, and culturally and socially-determined moral and ethical standards restricted what could and could not be seen on movie screens in American theaters.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Constructing Femininity: Women in Chinese Painting
courses.description: This course examines issues of femininity and sexuality in Chinese painting from the Han Dynasty (206 B.C.-220 A.D.) to the end of dynastic China in the nineteenth century. Course topics include the ways in which pictures of women help to craft the notion of femininity in pre-modern Chinese society and the differing roles of women as painters, patronesses, and collectors.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: The Invention of the Modern Artist
courses.description: This class examines the invention of the idea of the artist in the Western world, starting in Early Modernity and ending with the present. We consider the evolution of the artist's social status, the representation of the artist in a variety of media, shifting expectations for artistic training and community, the relationship between the artist and the art market, and different definitions of artistic genius or excellence in art marking.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: The City as Monument
courses.description: A city or cities will be considered as cultural artifact(s), with emphasis given to plans and planning, architecture, public monuments and to various institutions, such as religion, government, the arts, and commerce that initiate or affect these urban developments and forms. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Women in the Visual Arts II
courses.description: Discussion of topics related to the representation of women in Western art and/or women as producers of art.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Africa in the American Imagination
courses.description: Examines the ways African art appears in United States popular culture (advertisements, magazines, toys, films, art) to generate meanings about Africa. Addresses intersecting issues of nationalism, multiculturalism, imperialism, nostalgia, and race. Restricted to sophomores, juniors, and seniors.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Cathedrals, Abbeys, Castles: Gothic Art and Architecture, ca.1130-1500
courses.description: Covers the development of Gothic church and secular architecture in Europe between 1130 and 1500. Explores formal and constructive progress in architecture (including sculpture and stained glass windows) and social, political, and economic aspects of medieval society that affected these developments.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: City, Architecture, Art: Nuremberg as a European Artistic Center,1300-1600
courses.description: The course covers the development of art and architecture from ca. 1300 to ca. 1600 in one of the most important medieval and early modern art centers in Europe: Nuremberg, the hometown of the famous German painter Albrecht Dürer (1471-1528).
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ARTH 151; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Studies in the History of Graphic Art
courses.description: Required preparation, any intermediate art history course or permission of the instructor. Study of prints and printmaking in Western art from ca. 1400 to the present focusing on selected topics.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Greek Sculpture
courses.description: Required preparation, any intermediate art history course or permission of the instructor. A focused study of sculpture in Ancient Greece.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Greek Architecture
courses.description: A survey of Greek architectural development from the Bronze Age and Early Iron Age through the fourth century BCE. Special topics include the origins of monumental architecture, the development of the orders and architectural forms, and the role of the built environment in shaping cultural practices in the first millennium BCE.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, CLAR 268, CLAR 375, CLAR 244, or CLAR 492; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Roman Architecture
courses.description: The development of architecture in the Roman world from the ninth century BCE through the fourth century CE. The course focuses on the development of urbanism and the function, significance, and evolution of the main building types and their geographic distribution.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, CLAR 245, CLAR 247, or CLAR/ARTH 263; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

source.text: ARTH 465. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, CLAR 245, CLAR 247 , or CLAR/ARTH 263; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | CLAR 465 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: History of the Illuminated Book
courses.description: Chronological survey of major developments in book painting during the European Middle Ages from 300 to 1450 CE.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art of the Aztec Empire
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the art of the Aztec Empire, including architecture, monumental sculpture, small-scale sculpture, ceramics, painting, lapidary work, gold work, and feather work.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Northern European Art of the 14th and 15th Centuries
courses.description: Required preparation, any intermediate art history course or permission of the instructor. Advanced study of painting and sculpture in France, England, and the Netherlands, 1300 to 1400.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Early Modern Art, 1400-1750
courses.description: Required preparation, any intermediate art history course or permission of the instructor. This course explores specialized themes and/or broad topics in Western European art of the early modern period. Honors version available.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Early Modern and Modern Decorative Arts
courses.description: Required preparation, any intermediate art history course or permission of the instructor. This course traces major historical developments in the decorative and applied arts, landscape design, and material culture of Western society from the Renaissance to the present.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Roman Sculpture
courses.description: Survey of Roman sculpture (200 BCE-300 CE), including portraiture, state reliefs, funerary monuments, and idealizing sculpture, with emphasis on style, iconography, and historical development of sculpture in its sociocultural, political, and religious contexts.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, CLAR 245, CLAR 247 or CLAR/ARTH 263; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Roman Painting
courses.description: Surveys Roman painting from 200 BCE to 300 CE, with emphasis on style, iconography, historical development of painting in its sociocultural, political, and religious contexts. Treats current debates in scholarship.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art and Archaeology of Achaemenid Persia
courses.description: This course will examine the history and material culture of the ancient state known as the Achaemenid Persian Empire through ancient texts and archaeological sources. Beginning in the sixth century BCE, this ancient superpower ruled a vast and culturally diverse empire that stretched from Northern Libya to central Asia. Through an examination of key sites, objects, and texts we will explore the history and diversity of this multicultural empire.

source.text: ARTH 482. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | CLAR 482 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Culture on the Move: Art, Empire, and Restitution since 1800
courses.description: This discussion-based course examines the systems of value that confer special status on the broad category of cultural property, then explores a number of case studies of art theft and restitution since the early 19th century, with an emphasis on art theft during World War II and that undertaken under the aegis of European colonialism.

source.text: ARTH 484. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | HIST 468 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art of the Harlem Renaissance
courses.description: Examines the Harlem Renaissance (1918-1942) as an instance of both transnational modernism and cultural nationalism through study of how artworks articulate interrelated conceptions of race, gender, sexuality, and social class.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Contemporary African Art
courses.description: Examines modern and contemporary African art (1940s to the present) for Africans on the continent and abroad. Examines tradition, cultural heritage, colonialism, postcolonialism, local versus global, nationalism, gender, identity, diaspora.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, AAAD 101 or ARTH 152 or 155; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Special Topics in Art History
courses.description: Required preparation, any intermediate art history course or permission of the instructor. Selected topics in art history.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Monuments and Memory
courses.description: Explores the role of monuments in the formation of cultural memory and identity, both nationally and globally. Topics include the construction of identities in and through public spaces, commemoration of both singular individuals and ordinary citizens, and the appearance of new types of post-traumatic monuments in the 20th century.

source.text: ARTH 514. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | HIST 514 .

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Introduction to Museum Studies
courses.description: Introduces careers in museums and other cultural institutions. Readings and interactions with museum professionals expose participants to curation, collection management, conservation, exhibition design, administration, publication, educational programming, and fundraising.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: The Body in Social Theory and Visual Representation
courses.description: A study of how the human body has been represented in contemporary art and the relation of those representations to theories of the individual and society.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Urban Africa and Global Mobility
courses.description: The contemporary arts of Africa are framed by urbanization and global mobility. This course examines how artists examine, reflect on, and express visually experiences of these conditions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Art and Money
courses.description: This course explores intersection of art and economics from the 18th century to the present through themes such as value, markets, counterfeiting, and circulation. It examines money as a visual artifact and artworks that engage with monetary questions in the context of art history and Western economic theory.

source.text: ARTH 557. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST, COMMBEYOND.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Theories of Modern Art
courses.description: Required preparation, any intermediate art history course or permission of the instructor. A study of theoretical issues central to the understanding of trends in modern art (e.g., modernism, the avant-garde, formalism originality).

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Cultural Politics in Contemporary Art
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This course will examine strategies of critique in contemporary art. Organized thematically, it focuses on the tactics employed by artists who address political, social, or cultural issues through their work.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Current Issues in Art
courses.description: Addresses select issues that have gained or re-gained prominence in today's art world, for example globalization, training, the market, and the nature of the "contemporary."

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: History and Theory of Museums
courses.description: Required preparation, any intermediate art history course or permission of the instructor. Provides an historical overview of museums. Serves as an introduction to many of the theoretical issues museums face including: ethics, audiences, the role of museums in society, exhibiting dilemmas.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Experience in Research
courses.description: Required preparation, one 100-level art history course and one 200- to 399-level art history course. An experiential learning opportunity in independent and original research on a topic or in a field of the student's choosing under the close direction of a faculty supervisor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Honors in Art History
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Independent research directed by a faculty member leading to an honors thesis.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Honors in Art History
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Independent research directed by a faculty member leading to an honors thesis.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Advanced Readings Topics in the History of Art
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Museum Studies Apprenticeship
courses.description: Provides experience in some aspect of museum work: curatorial, educational, collections management, exhibition design, administration. Requires a minimum of 90 hours and will have an academic component.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ARTH 551 or ARTH 592; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: ARTH 755. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ARTH 551 or ARTH 592 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Colonialism and European Visual Culture, 1800-1990
courses.description: Considers the role of visual representation in the construction of European empire and its associated knowledges from the Napoleonic expedition to Egypt to debates over primitivism in the 1980s.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Greek Topography
courses.description: Study of chief archaeological sites of Greece and of existing buildings and monuments. Attention to the problems of excavation and the role of the sites in Greek history.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Methods in Art Historical Research
courses.description: This course introduces students to a variety of historical and contemporary methods for the interpretation of visual culture.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: alt-Methods: Digital Art History
courses.description: This course introduces students to current digital art history projects and practices as well as methods for approaching art historical research in new ways.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Professional Development
courses.description: This course focuses attention on the variety of ways in which scholars in the arts disseminate their research and market themselves. Students will analyze and participate in various weekly writing and oral exercises, but will focus on one specific genre for their semester long project.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Problems in the the History of Art
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Seminar in Chinese Art and Architecture
courses.description: Study selected topics in the history of Chinese art and architecture.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Seminar in Contemporary Global Arts
courses.description: This seminar examines contemporary artistic production that engages, questions, and challenges the narratives of culture and art that privilege Europe and America as the models for understanding cultural production.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Seminar in Latin American Art
courses.description: This seminar investigates topics in the history of colonial and modern Latin American Art.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Tudor and Jacobean Portraits: A Theoretical and Practical Investigation
courses.description: This course involves close and critical examination of a select body of extant portraits from the Tudor and Jacobean periods in English history (1485-1625) in the collection of the North Carolina Museum of Art. Students taking this unit will play an active role in researching these relatively unstudied works of art.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Mexico City: 1890-1950
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This course examines the visual culture of Mexico City between 1890 and 1950. It also considers works by artists outside of Mexico who were associated and inspired by cultural production here.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Seminar in Contemporary Art
courses.description: Addresses select topics and theoretical issues relevant to contemporary art.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Fashioning Power
courses.description: This graduate seminar focuses on fashion (clothing, accessories, style, performance) as the central cultural component for examining power in society.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Seminar in African American Art
courses.description: Advanced standing in art history or permission of the instructor. Explores current debates crucial to the study of African American art. Emphasis on the variety of theories and methods central to the field.

courses.subject: ARTH
courses.title: Graduate Writing Seminar
courses.description: Devoted to structuring an argument, assessing primary and secondary sources, and conducting a sustained writing exercise. The goal of the Graduate Writing Seminar is to produce a prospectus of the thesis by the end of the third semester. For Art History graduate students only.
